items.question:
An HR director at a 300-person manufacturing firm is designing a Claude Project for employee relations (ER) case management. She has identified four content types: (a) the ER policy manual — stable, approved, reviewed annually; (b) the employee roster with current employment status — updates daily; (c) case-specific correspondence for individual active ER cases; (d) a confidential legal advice note for a single sensitive current case. She has listed all four content types.

What should she do NEXT?

options.A: Add all four content types to Project knowledge to ensure the full HR team has maximum context for all ER work.
options.B: Add the ER policy manual and employee roster to Project knowledge and upload the case correspondence and legal note per-chat as needed.
options.C: Create four separate Projects, one per content type, to maintain clean data separation.
options.D: Add the ER policy manual to Project knowledge, configure a connector for the daily employee roster, and use per-chat uploads for the case-specific correspondence and the confidential legal advice note.

items.question: A tax director at a mid-market technology company is designing a Claude Project for the tax team. Which TWO documents are MOST appropriate for permanent Project knowledge? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The company's tax filing calendar listing key submission deadlines and responsible owners.
options.B: The draft tax provision model for the current year's financial close, still being reviewed by the CFO.
options.C: HMRC guidance on R&D tax relief, downloaded as a PDF from the government website.
options.D: Last quarter's tax working papers, which documented the methodology used for the Q3 provision.
options.E: An email thread between the tax manager and HMRC regarding a specific prior-year query.

items.question: A knowledge operations manager at a healthcare company is reviewing a shared Claude Project used by the clinical team. Which TWO observations are the STRONGEST indicators that the knowledge base needs curation? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The Project has been in active use for 12 months with no formally assigned curator.
options.B: Claude cited a hospital formulary that was superseded by a new edition six months ago as the current approved formulary.
options.C: The Project contains 15 documents, which the team considers a relatively large number.
options.D: Two documents named 'Formulary_2023.pdf' and 'Formulary_Current.pdf' exist in Project knowledge simultaneously.
options.E: The most recently uploaded document is a 100-page clinical reference manual.

items.question: A solutions architect at a fintech company is defining organisation-wide knowledge management principles for all Claude Projects. Which THREE principles MOST effectively prevent the most common Project knowledge failures? (Choose THREE)

options.A: When a document is updated, remove the prior version from Project knowledge in the same session.
options.B: Cap all Projects at 15 documents to prevent scope creep and maintain review manageability.
options.C: Use per-chat uploads exclusively to avoid ongoing lifecycle management obligations.
options.D: Configure connectors for knowledge sources that change daily or more frequently rather than using periodic static uploads.
options.E: Use per-chat uploads for documents that are sensitive, ephemeral, or specific to a single conversation or client engagement.

items.question: An IT governance team is establishing baseline rules for all shared Claude Projects used by cross-functional teams. Which TWO rules MOST directly prevent the most common shared Project failures? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Limit shared Projects to teams of fewer than 10 members to maintain accountability.
options.B: Before a document is added to a shared Project, confirm that all Project members are authorised to access it.
options.C: All documents in a shared Project must be relevant to the Project's defined use cases and applicable to most Project members' work.
options.D: Require IT governance approval and reapproval for all shared Projects on a six-month cycle.
options.E: Restrict shared Projects to a single document format to ensure consistent parsing.

items.question:
An HR coordinator at a 400-person logistics company drafts onboarding email templates using Claude. To provide context she pastes a row from the master employee spreadsheet containing the new hire's full name, home address, date of birth, and national ID number. The company's Claude account is a personal Pro subscription with no enterprise data-processing agreement.

Which field in the pasted row represents the HIGHEST-risk category of PII?

options.A: The employee's full name
options.B: The employee's national ID number
options.C: The employee's preferred first-name spelling
options.D: The department the employee is joining

items.question:
A clinical coordinator at a regional hospital uses Claude to draft a patient appointment reminder template. To show Claude the expected output format, she pastes a sample row from the scheduling system. The row includes: patient first name, diagnosis code, attending physician name, appointment date, and hospital department.

Which element of the sample row MOST directly qualifies the entire record as Protected Health Information requiring heightened handling?

options.A: The patient first name paired with the diagnosis code
options.B: The attending physician's name
options.C: The appointment date and time
options.D: The hospital department name

items.question:
A strategy consultant is using Claude to analyse a manufacturing client's supply chain inefficiencies. She has a 500-row vendor dataset ready to paste into the prompt. The dataset includes vendor name, country, transaction volumes, contract values, payment terms, and vendor account manager contact details (name, phone, email). The analysis only requires identifying underperforming vendor relationships by volume and cost.

Which approach BEST applies the data minimisation principle before submitting the dataset?

options.A: Submit the full dataset so Claude has maximum context for the analysis
options.B: Replace vendor names with codes but retain all other fields including contact details
options.C: Remove vendor contact details entirely, since they contribute nothing to the volume and cost analysis
options.D: Submit the full dataset but use an enterprise account so the contact details are contractually protected

items.question:
A credit risk analyst at a regional bank is drafting an internal memo assessing a commercial loan application. She plans to paste the loan application summary into Claude to help structure the memo. The summary includes the applicant's company name, annual revenue, credit score, debt-to-equity ratio, and Social Security Number. The bank's Claude deployment is an enterprise API account with a signed financial-data addendum.

What is the BEST practice for the Social Security Number before pasting?

options.A: Include it because the enterprise addendum explicitly permits processing financial PII
options.B: Display only the last four digits, following the standard masking convention for internal documents
options.C: Hash the SSN to a fixed-length token so it remains referenceable if needed later
options.D: Remove it entirely — it is not required to draft an assessment memo about business financials

items.question:
A data governance analyst at a health insurance company is reviewing a proposed Claude workflow that will process member records. Each record contains: (a) an insurer-assigned member ID number, (b) claim diagnosis codes for the current year, (c) the member's full legal name, (d) 5-digit ZIP code only, (e) preferred communication language. The analyst must identify the fields that require the most restrictive PHI-level handling.

Which TWO fields MOST directly constitute Protected Health Information requiring heightened controls? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Claim diagnosis codes for the current year
options.B: Preferred communication language
options.C: Full legal name paired with the insurer-assigned member ID
options.D: 5-digit ZIP code only

items.question:
A product manager at a 12-person e-commerce startup is building a Claude-powered customer service chatbot. During user testing, the team notices that some test users paste their full 16-digit credit card number into the chat when asking about a declined payment. The PM asks a developer whether this is a concern or whether it can be treated the same as any other personal data the chatbot collects.

What is the PRIMARY reason full credit card numbers require distinct handling beyond standard PII controls?

options.A: Credit card numbers are a subset of PII and should be treated identically to other personal identifiers
options.B: Payment card numbers fall under payment industry data standards — processing them through an uncertified channel creates specific compliance liability separate from general privacy obligations
options.C: Claude will automatically detect and refuse to process credit card numbers, so no additional controls are needed
options.D: Card numbers can be stored temporarily in the development environment since it is separate from the production system

items.question:
A management consultant at a mid-size advisory firm has been leading a due diligence engagement for a private equity client. She created a Claude Project and loaded it with the acquisition target's financial models, strategic plans, and draft synergy analyses — all shared under NDA. The engagement concluded last month. She is now starting a market-entry strategy project for an unrelated client in a different sector and opens the same Project to reuse the prompt templates she built.

What is the PRIMARY confidentiality risk in reusing the existing Project?

options.A: All documents loaded into the Project remain in the knowledge base and are accessible to Claude in every subsequent session within that Project, creating a structural pathway for prior-client data to surface in new work
options.B: Claude's conversation history from the prior engagement will automatically be included in every new session until the Project is deleted
options.C: The private equity client may detect the reuse through access logs shared under the enterprise agreement and claim a breach of confidentiality
options.D: The financial models will bias Claude toward financial analysis, degrading the quality of the market-entry strategy output

items.question:
A data scientist at a 12-person biotech startup uses her personal Claude.ai Pro subscription to analyse a patient cohort dataset. All direct identifiers — names, dates of birth, record numbers — have been removed. The remaining fields are age band (5-year ranges), diagnostic category, treatment arm, and outcome flag. A colleague argues the dataset is safe to process on the consumer account because no personal data remains.

What is the MOST significant gap in the colleague's argument?

options.A: Consumer accounts have lower context windows, which may truncate the dataset during analysis
options.B: Without direct identifiers, the dataset falls below the threshold for privacy regulation and requires no special handling
options.C: Removing direct identifiers does not eliminate re-identification risk — clinical quasi-identifiers can be combined with external data to re-identify individuals, and a consumer account without a DPA creates regulatory exposure regardless
options.D: The startup should deploy an on-premises model to ensure clinical data never leaves the company's infrastructure

items.question:
A paralegal at a 40-person litigation firm used a shared Claude Project to generate summaries of 80 deposition transcripts during a case that settled six months ago. The client relationship has ended. A new associate asks whether the Project and its documents can be repurposed for a different client matter beginning next week.

What is the FIRST action the firm should take before repurposing the Project?

options.A: Archive the Project to read-only status so the prior deposition summaries are preserved but inaccessible to active users
options.B: Transfer the reusable prompt templates to a new Project and leave the document library intact for reference
options.C: Confirm the summaries do not contain privileged strategy content, then repurpose the Project immediately
options.D: Review the engagement's data retention obligations, execute the required deletion of all prior-matter documents, and only then repurpose the Project

items.question:
A clinical operations coordinator at a pharmaceutical company is designing a Claude-assisted workflow to process patient adverse event reports. She has confirmed: (1) the fields required are event type, drug code, patient age range, and outcome flag; (2) the company's enterprise API account has a signed DPA; (3) the API connection has been tested and is working correctly. She is now ready to draft the system prompt.

What should she do NEXT?

options.A: Submit a test batch of five real adverse event reports to validate that Claude parses the fields correctly before finalising the system prompt
options.B: Define which fields in source reports should be redacted or tokenised before data reaches Claude, so minimisation is designed into the workflow before the first live prompt
options.C: Draft the system prompt first and add data minimisation controls in a later iteration once the output format is confirmed
options.D: Escalate to IT to upgrade the account to a higher model tier to ensure maximum accuracy for clinical adverse event data

items.question:
A procurement manager at a UK-headquartered retailer uses an enterprise Claude account to analyse supplier contracts. The company's legal team discovers that the API routes all requests through servers located in the United States. The retailer's suppliers include EU-resident sole traders whose names, addresses, and tax identifiers appear in the contracts.

What is the PRIMARY concern the legal team is identifying?

options.A: Transferring personal data about EU and UK individuals to servers in a jurisdiction without equivalent data-protection standards may breach cross-border transfer obligations under GDPR-style frameworks
options.B: API routing through US servers will add latency that materially degrades the analyst's user experience
options.C: Anthropic's US infrastructure lacks the ISO certification required to process EU commercial data
options.D: Supplier contract data is commercially confidential and prohibited from leaving UK jurisdiction under competition law

items.question:
A compliance officer at a US financial services firm is assessing a proposed Claude workflow to process customer records containing: full name, Social Security Number, brokerage account balance, trading history, and healthcare Flexible Spending Account (FSA) transaction data. She must identify which regulatory frameworks are MOST directly triggered.

Which TWO regulatory-style obligations are MOST directly implicated by the presence of SSNs and FSA transaction data specifically? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Export control obligations, because financial and health data cannot leave US jurisdiction under federal export rules
options.B: Health information privacy obligations apply to FSA transaction data because it constitutes health-related financial information linked to medical expenditures
options.C: PCI-DSS applies to the brokerage account balance because it constitutes stored financial account data
options.D: Financial privacy obligations analogous to Gramm-Leach-Bliley apply to the SSN and account data as nonpublic personal financial information
options.E: Anti-money laundering reporting obligations are triggered because trading history must be monitored for unusual patterns

items.question:
A bid manager at a professional services firm is drafting a response to a government RFP. She pastes the firm's internal pricing model — including labour-cost rates by grade, internal margin targets by service line, and partner billing rates — into Claude to help draft the commercial section. She is using a personal Claude.ai account because her enterprise account access expired.

What characteristic of the pasted data makes using a personal account MOST problematic?

options.A: The pricing model contains numerical formulas that Claude may misinterpret on a consumer-tier account
options.B: Government procurement rules prohibit use of AI tools on RFP responses
options.C: Internal pricing models are commercially confidential — a consumer account lacks the contractual controls that prevent inputs from being used to improve the model
options.D: The document is likely too large for a consumer-tier context window and will be truncated

items.question:
A senior consultant is six months into an engagement with a global investment bank. She has built a detailed Claude Project containing the bank's internal strategic roadmap, cost optimisation scenarios, and three shortlisted M&A targets — all provided under NDA. A partner now asks her to use the same Project to prepare a pitch deck for a prospective client that is a direct competitor of the bank.

What is the MOST significant risk if she proceeds as requested?

options.A: The bank's confidential strategic documents in the Project knowledge base are structurally accessible in every session within that Project, making it impossible to prevent cross-contamination of the NDA-protected material
options.B: The bank may identify the conflict through usage analytics shared under the enterprise agreement and escalate to the firm's leadership
options.C: The pitch deck will be inadvertently biased toward the incumbent bank's strategic perspective, reducing its effectiveness for the prospective client
options.D: The partner's instruction constitutes a direct NDA breach since the pitch is for a competing entity and the NDA explicitly prohibits any secondary use

items.question:
A data analyst at a large insurance company is writing a Python function to calculate premium loading factors from actuarial loss ratio tables. To give Claude sufficient context, she plans to paste the full policyholder database — 1.8 million rows including policyholder names, home addresses, dates of birth, and health questionnaire responses — into the prompt, reasoning that it is faster than extracting just the actuarial columns.

Which data governance principle does this approach MOST directly violate?

options.A: Purpose limitation — using health questionnaire responses for a premium calculation function constitutes secondary processing beyond the original collection purpose
options.B: Accuracy — pasting raw database rows risks introducing typographical errors that will corrupt the calculated loading factors
options.C: Accountability — the analyst is taking a governance action without formal approval from the data governance committee
options.D: Data minimisation — the coding task requires only actuarial columns, not the full personal database; submitting 1.8 million rows of personal data for a calculation task far exceeds what is necessary

items.question:
A legal operations manager at an insurance company needs to use Claude to summarise 300 claim files for a coverage dispute analysis. Each file contains: claimant name, policy number, medical diagnosis, legal strategy notes prepared by outside counsel, and settlement amount. The team wants maximum analytical value while minimising data exposure and privilege risk.

Which TWO actions BEST address the data exposure and privilege risks before submitting the files? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Submit the files without redaction since the enterprise account prohibits Anthropic from using inputs for training
options.B: Replace claimant names with sequential identifiers such as Claimant-001 before submitting
options.C: Remove legal strategy notes from each file, since they carry attorney-client privilege risk independent of the PII concern
options.D: Use a consumer account for this task since legal content requires unrestricted processing capability
options.E: Convert all PDFs to plain text first, which will strip embedded metadata from the files

items.question:
A hospital IT director is evaluating a Claude API integration for nursing staff to draft care plan summaries. The workflow will pass patient name, date of birth, diagnosis, and current medications to the API. The vendor has confirmed it offers HIPAA-relevant technical controls — encryption at rest and in transit, access logging, and role-based access — and is willing to sign a Business Associate Agreement.

What obligation does the BAA create that the technical controls alone do NOT satisfy?

options.A: The BAA transfers all HIPAA compliance responsibility to the vendor, relieving the hospital of covered-entity obligations for this workflow
options.B: The BAA creates contractual accountability — it defines permitted uses of PHI, allocates liability, and obligates breach notification — obligations that exist in addition to, not instead of, the technical safeguards
options.C: The BAA certifies that the AI will not generate clinically inaccurate information, since it commits the vendor to output accuracy standards
options.D: The BAA automatically extends the hospital's existing Notice of Privacy Practices to cover AI processing, eliminating the need for additional patient disclosure

items.question:
A cloud architect at a European government agency is evaluating an enterprise Claude API deployment for processing citizen service applications. The agency's policy requires all data containing citizen records to remain within the EU. The vendor's standard API routes all requests through US-based infrastructure.

What is the PRIMARY control the agency should require before approving the deployment?

options.A: End-to-end AES-256 encryption for all data in transit, which neutralises jurisdiction concerns by making the data unreadable during transmission
options.B: A data-processing agreement that permits US processing provided standard contractual clauses are in place as a transfer safeguard
options.C: A contractual and technical commitment that citizen data is processed exclusively on EU infrastructure, not merely protected in transit to a non-EU location
options.D: Annual third-party audits of the US data centre confirming GDPR-equivalent security controls are maintained

items.question:
A fintech startup is building a Claude-powered loan underwriting assistant. Applicant records contain: employment status, postal code, self-reported religious affiliation from a voluntary diversity survey, monthly bank statement transactions, and credit bureau score. Legal counsel has flagged two fields as warranting heightened protection beyond standard PII controls.

Which TWO fields MOST likely triggered legal counsel's concern? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Credit bureau score, because it is a derived attribute and therefore exempt from standard PII protections
options.B: Religious affiliation, because it is a protected characteristic subject to special-category data rules under GDPR-style frameworks
options.C: Employment status, because it is a sensitive workplace record protected under labour law privacy obligations
options.D: Monthly bank statement transactions, because they constitute nonpublic personal financial data subject to sector-specific financial privacy obligations
options.E: Postal code, because statistical methods can infer ethnicity or socioeconomic status from geographic data

items.question:
A freelance UX researcher working from home uses her personal Claude.ai subscription to analyse 500 user interview transcripts from a study she conducted for a Fortune 500 client. The transcripts include participant first names, age ranges, occupations, and verbatim quotes about their health insurance experiences. The client contract requires all research data to be handled under a signed data-processing agreement.

What is the MOST significant compliance gap in the researcher's current approach?

options.A: Consumer accounts produce lower-quality qualitative analysis than enterprise deployments
options.B: The researcher should organise the transcripts in a Project rather than uploading them as individual files
options.C: Verbatim participant quotes must be anonymised before AI processing regardless of account tier
options.D: A personal Claude.ai account operates under consumer service terms without a data-processing agreement, directly violating the client contract's data-handling requirement

items.question:
A pharmacy technician at an independent chemist uses her personal Claude.ai account to draft patient counselling notes. She pastes the patient's first name, prescription drug name, dosage, and refill schedule into the prompt. A colleague says this is fine because the patient's surname, address, and date of birth were not included.

What is the MOST accurate assessment of the colleague's claim?

options.A: The colleague is correct — without a surname and date of birth, the record does not meet the threshold for protected health information
options.B: The colleague is wrong — a first name combined with a prescription drug and dosage links an individual to health information, constituting PHI regardless of whether a surname is present
options.C: The colleague is correct because pharmacy data is classified as financial data under PCI rules, not health data under HIPAA-style frameworks
options.D: The colleague is wrong because prescription data is always PCI-regulated regardless of how much identifying information accompanies it

items.question:
A clinical research associate at a pharmaceutical company prepares a patient dataset for a Claude-assisted analysis. She replaces every patient name and medical record number with a unique study code (e.g., PT-0047) and stores the code-to-identity mapping table in a separate encrypted database accessible only to the principal investigator.

How should this dataset be classified?

options.A: Pseudonymised — the codes can be re-linked to identities using the mapping table, so individuals remain identifiable to those with access to the key
options.B: Anonymous — once names and record numbers are replaced with codes, no personal data remains in the dataset
options.C: Encrypted — applying a reversible transformation to identifiers is the definition of encryption, not pseudonymisation
options.D: De-identified by safe harbour — replacing names and record numbers satisfies all requirements for formal de-identification

items.question:
An HR analytics team at a 20,000-person retailer collected detailed employee onboarding survey data — including commute distance, household income band, and dependent care arrangements — to improve the onboarding experience. The marketing analytics team has now requested access to the same dataset to segment employees for an internal product-testing panel.

Which data governance principle does the proposed repurposing MOST directly implicate?

options.A: Data accuracy — the onboarding survey data may have become stale and inaccurate since collection
options.B: Data minimisation — the marketing team should only receive the fields relevant to product testing
options.C: Purpose limitation — data collected under one stated purpose cannot be repurposed for a materially different use without a new legal basis
options.D: Retention — the onboarding survey data may have exceeded its permissible retention period

items.question:
A legal operations team at an insurer is processing 500 claim files through Claude to identify coverage patterns across claimants who have made multiple claims over three years. Each file contains a claimant's full name and a unique claim reference number. The analysis requires tracking which files belong to the same individual across multiple claims.

Which technique BEST balances the competing needs of minimising personal data exposure and preserving the ability to cross-reference files?

options.A: Anonymise all files by removing both the claimant name and the claim reference number before submission
options.B: Submit the full files including names so Claude can generate accurate cross-claimant pattern analysis
options.C: Redact the claimant name and submit only the claim reference number, which provides sufficient cross-file linkage
options.D: Replace claimant names with a consistent pseudonym token (e.g., CLM-10047) applied identically across all files belonging to the same individual, preserving cross-file linkage without exposing real identities

items.question:
A health-tech startup has a five-person team. Three team members access Claude via an enterprise API account with a signed DPA. Two team members use personal Claude.ai subscriptions because their enterprise seats have not been provisioned yet. The team is building a patient-intake summarisation workflow and has begun testing with real patient records.

Which TWO risks arise MOST directly from the mixed consumer-and-enterprise account configuration? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Patient data submitted through the personal accounts enters a consumer data pipeline without contractual data-handling protections, undermining the DPA the enterprise account provides
options.B: The personal-account users will receive lower-quality model outputs, degrading the overall workflow results
options.C: The enterprise account's DPA retroactively covers data processed by the personal accounts since the startup holds a single corporate relationship with the vendor
options.D: Regulatory auditors examining the workflow may find it impossible to demonstrate consistent data-handling controls across all team members, creating a documentation and accountability gap
options.E: Personal accounts have smaller context windows, preventing the personal-account users from processing full patient records

items.question:
An HR analytics lead at a 500-person manufacturing firm is preparing an employee dataset for a Claude-assisted engagement survey analysis. After removing employee names and ID numbers, the remaining fields are age (exact year), job title, department, and salary to the nearest £1,000. A colleague notes that one employee in the Procurement department holds a unique combination of job title and salary band that makes her the only person matching that description in the company.

What data privacy concept does this scenario illustrate?

options.A: Direct identifier exposure — salary to the nearest £1,000 is a direct personal identifier equivalent to a name
options.B: Re-identification via quasi-identifiers — a combination of non-identifying fields can uniquely describe an individual even after direct identifiers are removed
options.C: Purpose limitation — the salary data was collected for payroll purposes and cannot be used in survey analysis
options.D: Data accuracy risk — approximate salary figures introduce errors that compromise the analysis

items.question:
A customer service manager at a regional bank is reviewing which data categories analysts may use with the bank's enterprise Claude account. The team regularly works with: customer account balances, transaction histories, loan application statuses, and — occasionally — customer-provided credit card numbers when resolving payment disputes.

Which data element requires the MOST distinct handling regime beyond the bank's standard enterprise financial-data controls?

options.A: Customer-provided credit card numbers, because they fall under PCI-DSS — a separate payment-card standard with certification, tokenisation, and logging requirements that go beyond general financial privacy controls
options.B: Loan application statuses, because they constitute credit decision data regulated more strictly than transaction history
options.C: Account balances, because balance data is more sensitive than transaction history under financial privacy frameworks
options.D: Transaction histories, because they reveal spending patterns and are classified as special-category data under GDPR-style frameworks

items.question:
A medical researcher at a teaching hospital has a dataset of 400 patients diagnosed with a rare neurological condition. After removing names, dates of birth, addresses, and medical record numbers, the remaining fields are: disease subtype (one of 4 possible variants), year of diagnosis, treatment protocol (one of 3 options), and outcome (5-point scale). A colleague argues the dataset now meets the standard for anonymised research data since all direct identifiers have been removed.

What is the MOST significant flaw in the colleague's claim?

options.A: The outcome scale includes five points, which makes the data too granular to qualify as anonymised under safe-harbour rules
options.B: Removing four categories of identifier satisfies only partial de-identification; at least eight categories must be removed for formal anonymisation
options.C: Medical research datasets require expert statistical certification of anonymisation, not just identifier removal, regardless of what fields are present
options.D: In a small rare-disease cohort, the combination of subtype, diagnosis year, and treatment protocol may uniquely describe individuals — formal anonymisation requires demonstrating that no combination of remaining fields identifies any individual

items.question:
A commercial solicitor at a 30-partner law firm uses the firm's enterprise Claude account — covered by a signed DPA — to draft contractual advice for a client's acquisition. The DPA confirms Anthropic will not train on inputs and will not share client data with third parties. A trainee asks whether the DPA means the matter is fully covered from a confidentiality standpoint.

What is the MOST accurate response to the trainee's question?

options.A: Yes — the DPA establishes all necessary confidentiality protections since it prohibits both training and third-party disclosure
options.B: No — the DPA governs the vendor's data-handling obligations, but solicitor-client confidentiality is a separate professional obligation the solicitor must independently assess before sharing client matter details with any third-party system
options.C: Yes — solicitor-client confidentiality automatically extends to AI vendors under the DPA's third-party disclosure restriction
options.D: No — law firms cannot use AI tools for client work under any circumstances without explicit client consent to AI involvement

items.question:
A data analyst at a regional government health authority has been handed a new dataset by the IT team for use in a Claude-assisted population health analysis. The dataset was compiled from three source systems. The IT team confirms the API connection and enterprise account are properly configured. The analyst has a general idea of the analysis she wants to conduct but has not yet examined the dataset's contents or schema.

What should the analyst do FIRST before writing any prompts or submitting any data to Claude?

options.A: Draft the analysis prompts so they are ready to test as soon as the data classification is complete
options.B: Submit a small sample of the dataset to Claude to confirm the API connection handles the file format correctly
options.C: Examine the dataset schema and a representative sample to classify what data types are present, so appropriate minimisation and handling controls can be determined before any data is submitted
options.D: Request that IT upgrade the dataset to an encrypted format before any analysis begins

items.question:
A people analytics lead at a multinational technology company is expanding a Claude-powered workforce analysis workflow from UK employees to include EU-based staff. The legal team confirms that Standard Contractual Clauses are in place between the company and the AI vendor for the cross-border transfer of employee data from the EU to the vendor's US processing infrastructure.

Which additional step do SCCs require of the data exporter that an adequacy decision would NOT?

options.A: The data exporter must conduct a Transfer Impact Assessment to evaluate whether the destination country's laws undermine the protections guaranteed by the SCCs
options.B: The data exporter must obtain explicit consent from each EU employee before their data is transferred under the SCCs
options.C: The data exporter must apply end-to-end encryption that the destination-country government cannot legally compel the vendor to decrypt
options.D: The data exporter must register the transfer with the EU supervisory authority before processing begins

items.question:
An audit manager at a professional services firm is closing a three-year client engagement. The engagement's Claude Project knowledge base contains three document types: (1) client-provided financial statements (the firm's engagement letter specifies a 7-year retention requirement), (2) AI-generated working-paper drafts created by the team (firm policy: delete upon engagement close), (3) regulatory filings submitted during the engagement (statutory 6-year retention applies). She must execute the correct retention actions immediately.

Which TWO actions should she take NOW upon engagement close? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Delete the AI-generated working-paper drafts from the Project in accordance with the firm's deletion-on-close policy
options.B: Delete the client financial statements immediately since the engagement has concluded and client data should not be retained
options.C: Transfer the client financial statements and regulatory filings out of the Claude Project and into the firm's document management system under their respective retention tags
options.D: Archive the entire Project to read-only status and reassess all documents at the annual retention review
options.E: Request client approval before transferring any engagement documents to the firm's document management system

items.question:
A CTO at a 30-person fintech startup is reviewing which types of information the team should not submit to Claude via personal accounts. She lists: customer transaction records, source code for the firm's core risk model, employee salary data, and public API documentation. She tells the team that only source code is 'intellectual property, not personal data, so it is fine on a personal account.'

What is the MOST significant error in the CTO's reasoning?

options.A: Source code is also personal data under GDPR because it may contain developer names in comments
options.B: Public API documentation is commercially confidential and should not be submitted to any Claude account
options.C: The confidentiality obligation for commercially sensitive IP (source code) is independent of whether it is personal data — a personal account's consumer terms create risk for trade secrets as well as for PII
options.D: The CTO is correct that source code is not personal data and therefore has no restrictions on which Claude account tier can process it

items.question:
A head of analytics at a large retail loyalty program is considering whether a customer dataset can be treated as low-sensitivity for a Claude workflow. The dataset has had names, emails, and phone numbers removed. It retains: age in years, gender, postcode sector, purchase frequency, and top three product categories. The team plans to combine this dataset with a third-party demographic enrichment file to improve segmentation.

What risk does the planned combination MOST directly create?

options.A: Combining the datasets will increase the file size beyond what the enterprise account can process efficiently
options.B: The third-party enrichment file may not be covered by the existing DPA, creating a contractual gap for the combined dataset
options.C: Product category data is a special category under GDPR because it may reveal health-related purchase patterns
options.D: Joining the pseudonymised retail dataset with a third-party demographic file may re-identify individuals by creating a richer quasi-identifier combination that narrows records to specific people

items.question:
A digital product manager at a health-tech company is designing a workflow in which Claude processes users' self-reported mental health diary entries to generate personalised wellbeing tips. The legal team asks the product manager to confirm the legal basis for processing this special-category health data. The PM argues that users tick a box when they sign up, so consent is established.

What additional requirement does valid consent for processing special-category data impose that the PM's tick-box approach may not satisfy?

options.A: Consent for special-category data must be renewed annually to remain valid
options.B: Special-category data can only be processed under a statutory public-interest basis — consent is never a valid legal ground for health data
options.C: Consent for special-category data must be explicit — the user must clearly affirm agreement to the specific processing of sensitive data, not merely accept general terms
options.D: Special-category data consent requires a countersignature from a qualified clinician confirming the user understands the implications

items.question:
An HR director at a 5,000-person global company is preparing employee grievance files for a Claude-assisted pattern analysis. Each file contains employee name, ID, department, grievance category, HR manager's notes, and the decision outcome. A data protection officer reviews the proposed redaction approach, which removes employee ID numbers and replaces manager names with initials. The DPO concludes the redaction is insufficient.

Which TWO elements of the proposed redaction approach are MOST likely driving the DPO's concern? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Removing employee ID numbers alone does not protect the employees' identities since employee names remain in the files
options.B: The grievance category and decision outcome may constitute sensitive employment data requiring removal rather than retention
options.C: Replacing manager names with initials does not anonymise managers who are the sole holder of a unique initial pair in the department
options.D: Grievance files cannot legally be used for pattern analysis under employment law, regardless of the redaction approach
options.E: HR manager notes should be converted to numerical codes before submission to reduce their token count

items.question:
An infrastructure architect at a community hospital is deploying a Claude API integration for clinical documentation. The vendor has signed a Business Associate Agreement, and the integration has been approved by the compliance team. However, the development team skipped implementing audit logging on the API calls because the sprint timeline was tight. They argue the BAA already covers HIPAA compliance.

What is the MOST accurate assessment of the compliance gap?

options.A: The BAA is sufficient — once the vendor has signed it, the hospital's obligations for this workflow are satisfied
options.B: The development team is correct that the BAA covers HIPAA obligations, but a separate GDPR-compliance gap exists for EU patient data
options.C: The compliance team's approval was premature; no BAA is legally valid without audit logging already implemented at the time of signing
options.D: A BAA governs the vendor's obligations, not the hospital's technical safeguard requirements — audit logging is a covered-entity control the hospital must implement independently of the BAA

items.question:
A benefits manager at a 3,000-person manufacturing employer runs a voluntary employee wellness program. Participants submit weekly mood and energy self-assessments through an app. The data is held by the employer, not a health plan or healthcare provider. The benefits team wants to use Claude to analyse aggregate trends in the wellness data.

What is the PRIMARY data handling consideration the benefits manager should assess BEFORE proceeding?

options.A: Whether individual employees can be identified from the wellness data, given that individually identified health-related data held by an employer may trigger privacy obligations even outside a formal healthcare context
options.B: Whether the wellness app's terms of service permit the employer to export data for analytics purposes
options.C: Whether the enterprise Claude account has sufficient context window capacity to process 3,000 employees' weekly submissions
options.D: Whether the mood and energy data qualifies as biometric data, which would require a separate biometric data processing agreement

items.question:
A data scientist at a financial services firm is building a Claude-assisted anomalous expense claim detection workflow. Source records include: employee ID, expense category, amount, date, merchant name, employee's home country, employee's performance rating, and employee's salary band. Privacy counsel identifies two fields that should be removed under data minimisation before the records are submitted to Claude.

Which TWO fields should be removed? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Expense amount, because it is a financial data point that creates PCI-DSS obligations
options.B: Employee performance rating, because it has no analytical relevance to expense anomaly detection and introduces unnecessary sensitive employment data
options.C: Employee salary band, because it is not required to identify anomalous expense claims and constitutes sensitive personal financial data
options.D: Employee home country, because it may be needed to contextualise local expense norms and currency thresholds
options.E: Merchant name, because it identifies a commercial entity rather than a person and should be excluded from personal data processing

items.question:
A project manager at a legal technology firm has been using a Claude Project to manage documentation for a software development contract with a large law firm client. The contract signed two years ago specifies a 5-year retention period for all project records. The development work was completed and formally signed off eight months ago, though invoicing continued until three months ago.

From which event does the 5-year retention period MOST likely begin under standard contract and professional records principles?

options.A: From the date the contract was signed two years ago
options.B: From the date the project was formally signed off as complete eight months ago
options.C: From the date the final invoice was settled three months ago, as this represents the conclusion of all financial obligations under the contract
options.D: From today's date, since the retention clock starts when the organisation first reviews its retention obligations

items.question:
A procurement coordinator at a 600-person manufacturer has been using her personal Claude.ai account to analyse supplier NDA terms and pricing proposals. The company has an enterprise Claude account for exactly this type of work, but she finds the personal account faster to access from her home office. Her manager discovers this when reviewing her files.

What is the PRIMARY concern the manager should raise?

options.A: Commercially sensitive supplier pricing and NDA terms were processed under consumer account terms, without the contractual data-handling protections the enterprise account provides
options.B: Personal accounts produce less accurate contract analysis than enterprise accounts
options.C: NDA terms and pricing data are not personal data, so there is no regulatory concern with using a personal account
options.D: The employee may have inadvertently accepted the supplier's terms by pasting them into an AI tool

items.question:
An HR administrator at a university is preparing an employee performance dataset for a Claude-assisted analysis. She removes employee ID numbers from the spreadsheet before pasting it into the prompt. The remaining fields include employee full name, department, tenure, performance score, and salary band. She believes the dataset is now appropriately de-identified.

What has gone wrong with this redaction approach?

options.A: Salary band is a special-category attribute that must be encrypted before processing, regardless of other redaction steps
options.B: Employee ID numbers are a secondary identifier — removing them while retaining full names leaves the primary personal identifier intact, making the redaction effectively meaningless
options.C: The dataset still contains department information, which is a quasi-identifier that could enable re-identification
options.D: Tenure is a time-based field that can be combined with public LinkedIn data to re-identify individuals

items.question:
A fintech startup's enterprise Claude API account is covered by a DPA that specifies the processing of customer payment transaction data for fraud-detection purposes. Without informing the legal team, the HR team begins using the same API account to process employee performance reviews, compensation analyses, and disciplinary records.

What is the PRIMARY data governance gap created by the HR team's actions?

options.A: The HR team is using a fraud-detection account for a non-fraud task, which will degrade the quality of both workflows
options.B: Employee data is a special category under GDPR, which automatically prohibits processing it through any AI account regardless of DPA terms
options.C: Employee HR data is outside the DPA's defined scope — the vendor's data-handling obligations do not cover this new category, leaving it contractually unprotected
options.D: The HR team should have obtained employee consent before using the same API account that processes customer data

items.question:
A mental health app company processes users' daily mood logs and therapy session notes through Claude to generate personalised insights, relying on explicit user consent as the legal basis. A user exercises their right to withdraw consent. The product team acknowledges the withdrawal but continues using three months of the user's historical data already loaded into a Claude Project for the same analysis.

What obligation does the consent withdrawal MOST directly trigger?

options.A: The company must notify the relevant data protection authority within 72 hours of receiving the withdrawal request
options.B: The company may continue using historical data already collected since withdrawal only affects future data collection
options.C: The company must delete the user's data from the Project and cease all processing of their data, since consent was the sole legal basis and has been withdrawn
options.D: The company must cease all processing immediately and remove the user's data from all active workflows and stored datasets, since withdrawal of consent is retrospective when consent is the exclusive legal basis

items.question:
A hospital uses the Claude API for clinical documentation assistance. The enterprise account has a signed BAA with the API vendor. The hospital's technology team discovers that AI-generated documentation summaries are then automatically exported to a third-party business intelligence platform for departmental reporting. The BI platform has no BAA with the hospital.

Which TWO compliance gaps does this configuration MOST directly create? (Choose TWO)

options.A: The BI platform receives PHI without a signed BAA, making the hospital potentially liable for unsanctioned PHI disclosure to a business associate
options.B: Exporting AI-generated summaries is prohibited because AI outputs are never considered PHI regardless of their content
options.C: The Claude API's BAA automatically extends to all downstream systems that receive its outputs
options.D: The hospital, as the covered entity, is responsible for ensuring all parties that receive PHI in the workflow have valid BAAs — an obligation that currently extends to the BI platform
options.E: The BI platform must independently apply to become a covered entity before it can receive clinical data
